title: Interviewing Louis Armstrong in New York
summary: Russell interviews Armstrong near the Apollo and backstage at the Strand, plays him Ida Cox records, gets the new Decca catalog from Alpha, and asks about Bunk Johnson.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Let me move this mic a little closer to you. Your voice is soft.

Was Louis Armstrong in New York at this time playing with... Well he was traveling all around. I actually interviewed him for the book up at the, I think it was up above the Apollo Theater or someplace in that block where they were having a rehearsal. I see. And then poor Louis wanted to play the Cavalieria Rusticana. What do they call it?

intermezzo comes between acts or something there in the opera just a slow number in 3-4 time it isn't a waltz or anything just a slower thing than that and he had a very nice arrangement that he was doing and playing the melody more or less straight and Joe Glazer had an assistant there, Joe Glazer was still his manager, was already his manager had been for years I guess even then so finally his manager told him he couldn't use that number gee Louie was so mad he said someday I'm going up there and tell those so and so's what to do anyway one day at least I interviewed him unfortunately didn't get it recorded and another day was backstage at the Strand Theatre it was a Broadway movie theatre that had stage shows usually just a band or a singer and all not any elaborate thing like say the Radio City or Rock City or anything but Louie was a featured band one week so I went backstage and got to talk to him quite a while funny thing I was also working on a discography of Louie for Downbeat which Paul Edward Miller had organized and put together and published under his name actually so after I took a lot of records and a little machine along to play records for Louie especially some of the I remember the Ida Cox records on Paramount which had some of us confused we couldn't tell for sure if it was Louie or not so like I'd played one of the Ida Cox I forget the one that was most likely and seemed like it might have had Lonesome in the title but I'm not sure and he began shaking his head and then all of a sudden he said oh no no no no not me it must be Tommy well I wouldn't do that or something but the tone and all and the style sounded a whole lot like Louie although usually Tommy Ladner was playing a lot of muted things and preaching he was famous as a preaching trumpet as they call it in the Paramount ads at that particular period
